title: Relative clauses: the people who rise up

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and *quien* from B1 Unit 5. They tell us which people or things we mean. To explain what a revolution is, they are very useful: *the military who take power*, *the rulers who lose support*.

items.spanish: Los militares que toman el poder cambian al gobernante.
items.english: The military who take power change the ruler.

items.spanish: Los gobernantes que tienen el poder pierden el apoyo del ejército.
items.english: The rulers who hold power lose the army's support.

items.spanish: Las personas que se sublevan quieren un cambio profundo.
items.english: The people who rise up want a deep change.

items.spanish: Algunas revoluciones cambiaron las empresas que eran del Estado.
items.english: Some revolutions changed the companies that belonged to the state.

sections.content: For people you can use *que* (*los militares que toman el poder*) in a clause that says which ones. In English you say "who" for people and "that" for things; Spanish uses *que* for both.
